scope: New bounded five-stage FFT DIF arithmetic component; no SDK dispatch or performance claim at this stage
hypothesis: R260 headroom permits butterfly additions/subtractions to remain unreduced inside a 32-vector DIF tile, reducing correction passes before restoring the ordinary below-2p contract at the existing storage boundary.
mechanism: Five DIF stages only. A low output is an unreduced normalized-limb sum; a high output multiplies (2^(stage+1)*p+a-b) by a canonical root. Each high product returns below2p. End normalization uses the exact per-output bound determined by its trailing low branches, totaling31 conditional correction passes instead of80 per low output path. Root data, multiplication, FFT order and final representation are unchanged.
bounds: Uniform R=2^260, p<2^254, normalized input below2p and roots belowp. Intermediate additions below64p<R. Product T<64p^2<pR gives REDC<p+T/R<2p. Signed add/subtract coefficients stay below2^58 conservatively. All32 outputs normalized below2p before compact/get or any external use. Unsupported MIXED/domain parameters assert rather than silently using the new routine.

research.source_scope: Scott's indexed abstract and relevant excerpts motivate delayed reduction; full PDF returned403. The exact BN254/R260 five-stage schedule and bounds here are independently derived, not reported speedups from that paper.
research.prior_results: Prior native R260 buckets, bounded coordinate subtraction, fixed-factor FFT leaves, square/CIOS variants and serial FFT leaves remain unchanged; this introduces no table, operand preparation or scheduling change.

implementation_scope: Add one experimental uniform-field DIF32 routine and private helpers to the existing four-lane field source and generated eight-lane file. Ordinary methods unchanged. Isolated Rust driver compares the accepted exact field library with fresh-reference and new routine from one source. No heap allocation inside the routine, extra point array, persistent roots or new key storage.
correctness: Source recovery byte-for-byte after removing the new block in both four/eight-lane files; existing generator check.
All existing native field tests unfiltered.
Independent arbitrary-precision Montgomery/schedule model with raw limb equality and all intermediate bounds, including maximal lazy inputs and canonical root corners.
Independent Arkworks direct32-point Fourier oracle, including nonzero column twists at the actual component geometries, and four/eight lanes.
Raw output limbs normalized and value below2p; compact/expand roundtrip unchanged.
Every benchmark output word agrees across all variants in each paired block.

timing.order: Rotate cases/variants by block and reverse variant order on odd blocks.
timing.inside: Repeated changing-state full32-vector DIF tile, final optimizer barrier; no input packing, initial input creation, canonical output conversion or reporting.
timing.no_overlap: No other owned build, profile, benchmark or archive during unprofiled timing.

gate.primary_q256: Positive paired median gain against both controls and at least21/31winningblocks.
gate.three_case_aggregate: Geometric mean of the three paired case medians below1 against both controls and at least21/31winningblockaggregates.
gate.nonregression: Everycase pairedmedian <=1.03 against both controls; fresh-reference calibration withinfactor1.03 ofaccepted.
gate.policy: No minimum positive-gain floor, selective exclusion or unchanged retry. A failed component gate closes this implementation; a pass motivates a separately declared full-FFT/SDK integration and does not satisfy the full objective.

profiles: After all latency, one999Hzcycles:u q256 capture pervariant,5000000 tileiterations; --no-buildid-cache from first capture. Retain actual linked routines/callees and sample-loss audit. Profiles include setup/primes/output and are component observations only.
publication: Commit and push after this completed experiment, including a negative result. Preserve the accepted 170-file production source and qualified SDK. Full eight-shape CPU/Metal objective remains active.
